title: Ta'if: the hardest day
hook: He walked to another town to ask for help. They chased him out with stones. Then an angel offered revenge.

screens.text: **He walked to another town to ask for help.** They chased him out with stones. Then an angel offered him revenge. You met the ending on Day 73. This is the whole day.
**Looking for support.** After the Year of Sorrow, with Khadijah and Abu Talib gone, he went to the town of Ta'if. He invited its people to Islam and asked for their support [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen].
bubbles: Zayd ibn Harithah, the man he had freed and raised as a son, was with him, one account says [Yaqeen].

screens.prompt: What had he lost just before going to Ta'if? Pick all that apply.

options.feedback: Yes. She had died that year, after about 25 years of marriage.
Yes. With Abu Talib gone, Makkah grew harsher, and he looked elsewhere for support.
Not quite. He went to Ta'if still calling people to Allah. His grief never became giving up.

screens.text: **Stones on the road.** The people of Ta'if refused him and insulted him. Then they set people on him who threw stones until his feet bled [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen].
bubbles: Zayd was hurt trying to shield him, according to that same account [Yaqeen].

events.title: To Ta'if
events.text: He goes to invite its people and seek support [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen].

events.title: Refused
events.text: A leader there turns him away, and people throw stones until his feet bleed [IslamQA 11575; Bukhari 3231].

events.title: Walking in grief
events.text: He walks on, overwhelmed, until a cloud shades him [Bukhari 3231].

events.title: An offer
events.text: Jibril brings the angel of the mountains, who offers to crush the town [Bukhari 3231].

events.title: Hope
events.text: He refuses, hoping their descendants will worship Allah alone [Bukhari 3231].

screens.text: **His hardest day.** Years later, Aisha asked if he'd ever had a day harder than the battle of Uhud. He told her about this one: rejected, he walked on in grief until he looked up, saw a cloud shading him, and **Jibril** in it [Bukhari 3231].
bubbles: Jibril had brought the angel of the mountains, who offered to crush the town between two mountains [Bukhari 3231].

screens.prompt: Why did he say no to the angel's offer?

options.text: He hoped their descendants would worship Allah alone
options.feedback: Right. On his worst day, he looked past his own pain to their children [Bukhari 3231].
Not quite. He called it the hardest day of his life. He chose mercy anyway.

options.text: He planned to take revenge himself later
options.feedback: Not quite. He refused revenge, hoping their children would one day worship Allah [Bukhari 3231].

screens.text: **Answer hate with hope.** On his worst day, the Prophet ﷺ could have destroyed the people who hurt him. He chose to hope for their children instead. When people mock your faith, you don't have to answer in kind.

screens.situation: Ana's cousin leaves a cruel comment about Muslims under her photo, and a few relatives like it. Ana could screenshot it and expose him in the family group chat.

options.text: Don't retaliate; reply calmly or message him privately, and make du'a for him
options.feedback: Yes. That's the spirit of Ta'if: no revenge, and hope that he changes.

options.text: Expose him to the whole family
options.feedback: Not quite. Revenge might feel good for a minute, but it closes doors. He chose hope.

options.text: Block every relative who liked the comment
options.feedback: Not quite. Protect your peace if you need to, but don't cut off family over one moment.

Make a **du'a** (personal prayer) that Allah guides them and softens their heart

screens.text: On his hardest day, he was offered revenge and chose hope. Their children were worth waiting for.

options.text: To crush the town between two mountains
options.feedback: Right. He refused, hoping their descendants would worship Allah alone [Bukhari 3231].
Not quite. The angel offered to crush the town. He refused [Bukhari 3231].

check.prompt: What's the lesson of Ta'if for a new Muslim who's mocked?

options.text: You don't have to answer cruelty in kind; you can hope for the person
options.feedback: Right. He chose hope over revenge on his worst day.

options.text: Get even, so it doesn't happen again
options.feedback: Not quite. He had the power for revenge and refused it.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- After the Year of Sorrow he went to Ta'if to invite its people and seek support; they refused, insulted him, and set people on him who threw stones until his feet bled [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (How Muhammad Confronted Hate)].
- Zayd ibn Harithah was with him and was hurt shielding him (his head was gashed, Yaqeen says) [Yaqeen]. Single source: keep it "one account says".
- He told Aisha it was the hardest day of his life: rejected by Ibn 'Abd Yalil, he walked on in grief until a cloud shaded him and Jibril came with the angel of the mountains [Bukhari 3231].
- The angel offered to crush them between two mountains; he refused, hoping their descendants would worship Allah alone [Bukhari 3231].
- Note: Bukhari 3231 names the man, not the town, and calls it "the day of al-'Aqabah"; the link to Ta'if comes from the early biographers. Day 73 already teaches the angel's offer.

**Likely questions**
- *"What was the du'a he made after Ta'if?"* The well-known du'a ("To You I complain of my weakness…") is reported outside the six collections, and its chain is widely considered weak, so this track doesn't teach it as his words. Say it's "a well-known du'a whose chain scholars consider weak", and that anyone may pour out their heart to Allah in their own words. (scholar question Q43)
- *"Wasn't there a Christian servant who was kind to him there?"* The story of Addas is in the early biographies but hasn't been verified for this track, so it's left out; don't tell it as fact. (scholar question Q43)
- *"Did the people of Ta'if become Muslim later?"* Don't answer from memory. Say later episodes cover what happened, and that the hadith shows his hope for their descendants [Bukhari 3231].
- *"How do I respond when people mock my faith?"* Calm, brief, no revenge; protect your peace; make du'a for them. If it becomes harassment or threats, document it and get help (safety rule if there's danger). Day 71 and Day 73.

**Escalate:** threats or harassment that make a convert unsafe (safety rule, never only the imam queue).

**Don't**
- Don't quote the Ta'if du'a as his words.
- Don't tell the Addas story.
- Don't state as certain that Ibn 'Abd Yalil was "the leader of Ta'if"; keep the town link as the early biographers' account.
- No graphic detail of his injuries; don't picture the Prophet ﷺ, Zayd, Jibril or the angel of the mountains.
